transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09 16:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Marigold Head of Search), Omar Khalid (Infra), Priya Singh (ML), Tom Reed (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, rough):
- Marigold exploring where to run embeddings + rerank: hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated GPUs vs Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Key constraints: 80–150 QPS peak for product search, 512-dim embedding targets, latency SLO 60–120ms for rerank path, strict data residency + audit log needs.
- Next: benchmarking on Dedicated, share pricing + security docs, schedule infra deep dive.

Topics: hosting options, embedding dim/quantization, vector DB integration, fallback/hybrid search, throughput and tail latency, security and VPC, pricing & SLAs

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:04] Lena (Marigold): Lena here, Head of Search. We own product search and personalization.
[00:07] Omar (Marigold Infra): Omar, infra eng, I'll be focused on networking and infra constraints.
[00:10] Priya (Marigold ML): Priya, ML, embeddings and rerank pipeline owner.
[00:13] Tom (Marigold Security): Tom from security. I'll pepper in compliance Qs.
[00:16] Avery: Great. Samir and Maya are on from our solutions engineering side. We wanted to understand your current pipeline and constraints and then talk about choices—hosted, dedicated, or private.
[00:25] Samir (Redwood SE): Quick note, I might say things like KV cache as K-V or K V, transcriber sometimes flips names, so flagged.
[00:31] Priya: Happy with that. High level: we have ~10M SKUs, index of 30M variants, but search surface uses a pre-filtered candidate set so we expect mid-flight queries to probe ~100–200 vectors. We plan to serve two paths: a cheap nearest neighbor recall (approx 10ms) then an expensive rerank using a 512-dim transformer embed + cross encoder that needs low latency for top10.
[00:51] Avery: When you say cheap recall, where do you run your vector DB today?
[00:54] Priya: Currently prototype on a managed Milvus cluster in GCP but it's flaky at scale. We also test Pinecone for some use cases. Looking to standardize the embedding inference and rerank logic.
[01:03] Maya (Redwood): Got it. Do you generate embeddings in-line at query time or precompute?
[01:07] Priya: Precompute for product catalog vectors, but we also have contextual embeddings for session signals generated at request time — that pushes QPS requirements. Peak QPS for embeddings gen is about 80 sustained with spikes to 150 during sales events.
[01:18] Omar: Also note our networking constraint: we must keep production traffic inside our VPC for security and egress cost reasons, at least for PII-adjacent signals.
[01:28] Tom: SOC 2 Type II is a must, plus we need audit logs, KMS-managed keys, and optional on-prem airgap for certain EU customers.
[01:36] Samir: Sounds like Marigold is leaning towards either Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private. Quick framing: Hosted (Redwood API) is easiest to deploy and we manage models; Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with isolation and predictable throughput; Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane (VPC/on-prem). Each has tradeoffs on cost and operations.
[01:55] Lena: Cost is important. We have an internal target to not exceed X per query — I'll avoid exacts on the call — and latency targets of 60–120ms for rerank.
[02:04] Avery: Understood. Can you describe your rerank? Is it a full cross-encoder or a multi-stage?
[02:09] Priya: Multi-stage. First stage ANN top2k from vector DB, second stage a mid-sized cross encoder for top 50 candidates. Cross encoder uses context + user signals, models are quantizable to int8-ish for savings but we care about accuracy.
[02:22] Samir: For throughput, are you planning to run cross-encoder on the same path as your embedding gen? Or separate service?
[02:26] Priya: Separate service conceptually but co-located in the same infra so network hops are minimal. We'd like batching for the cross-encoder up to N=16 but have strict per-request latency SLO.
[02:37] Maya: That's a classic batching vs tail-latency trade. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and can be tuned by sequence length and batch windows. We also support hybrid routing: cheap recall in customer-hosted DB and rerank on Redwood Dedicated. That reduces token costs.
[02:51] Omar: If we host vector DB ourselves (Milvus on GKE), how does Redwood integrate? Do we need VPC peering or do you push vectors out?
[02:58] Samir: Integration patterns: 1) You keep vector DB in your VPC and call Redwood API (Hosted) for embeddings/rerank — traffic leaves VPC unless you use Redwood Private or Dedicated in same cloud region with VPC peering. 2) Dedicated can be deployed in your cloud region with VPC peering and restricted ingress. 3) Private gives you full control — we ship a private control plane and you manage the data plane.
[03:21] Omar: For peering, is it cross-cloud? We have multi-cloud strategy — some clusters in GCP, others in AWS.
[03:26] Maya: Dedicated deployed in a region works best if the DB and Redwood compute are co-located. Cross-cloud adds egress and latency. Private is more flexible for hybrid setups but requires more ops.
[03:36] Tom: What about key management? We need KMS/HSM integration and the ability to rotate keys without service interruption.
[03:42] Samir: We integrate with AWS KMS and GCP KMS, and for Private we support customer HSM workflows. Rotation can be coordinated; we provide docs for zero-downtime rotation patterns.
[03:51] Lena: On embeddings, we are experimenting between 384 and 1024 dims but leaning to 512. We worry about storage and index size — 512 dims increases index memory and query cost. Any guidance?
[04:03] Maya: Tradeoffs: higher dims yield better recall/precision, but cost scales roughly linearly in storage and query CPU. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization (8-bit) and we support compact float16 paths; also rerank can be used to keep recall dims low and push accuracy into the cross-encoder stage.
[04:20] Priya: Do you have benchmarks for 512-dim embeddings at 80 QPS with topK 100?
[04:25] Samir: We have internal benchmark templates — we'll run a Dedicated profile for that workload. For Hosted it's more variable because of multi-tenant effects. Dedicated gives predictable tail latencies.
[04:35] Omar: About caching, can Redwood do prefix or KV cache for ephemeral session vectors? We want to avoid regen on repeat queries.
[04:41] Maya: Yes, there is KV caching support — prefix caching for static items and session caching for ephemeral vectors. That reduces per-token compute and helps cost.
[04:50] Tom: How are logs and audit trails handled? We need immutable audit logs for model invocations and data access.
[04:55] Samir: We produce audit events for each request: model id, route, timestamp, and can stream those logs to your S3/GCS. For Private, logs can remain inside your environment only.
[05:05] Lena: For hybrid search, our idea is run ANN in Milvus for candidate recall then call Redwood for rerank. Does Redwood ingest vectors or just call out to DB for neighbor lookups?
[05:14] Priya: We're thinking about embedding sync — do we push vectors to Redwood so you can do end-to-end?
[05:19] Maya: Two patterns: 1) you host DB and call Redwood rerank with payload of candidate ids+metadata — Redwood doesn't need full vector set. 2) you push a subset (hot set) of vectors to Redwood Dedicated caching layer for lower latency rerank. Pushing the whole corpus is possible but has cost implications.
[05:35] Priya: Pushing hot set could be helpful for peak events. How does invalidation work for product churn? We change SKUs daily.
[05:42] Samir: We support incremental syncs and TTL-based invalidation. Syncs can be via S3+manifest or API push.
[05:48] Omar: Network egress costs matter—if we push vectors to Redwood Hosted in another cloud, that's expensive.
[05:53] Maya: Correct, that's why Dedicated/Private where compute is in-region is common for retail.
[05:59] Tom: Any considerations on PII? We sometimes include user IDs in query context.
[06:04] Samir: You can strip or hash PII before sending. For Private, data never leaves your VPC. For Hosted, we have data handling contracts and can restrict retention.
[06:13] Lena: On the model side, we want the ability to A/B test embeddings and rerank models across small cohorts. How do rollouts work?
[06:19] Maya: Redwood Console supports per-route model pinning and canary rollouts. You can route X% of traffic to a new model, and Console emits metrics for latency/cost/quality tied to prompt sets.
[06:30] Priya: Are evals integrated? We have an offline eval harness for relevance.
[06:34] Samir: We integrate with evaluation sets; Redwood Optimize can alert on regressions based on prompt set changes.
[06:39] Lena: Pricing — are there fixed costs for Dedicated? We may need reserved capacity for Black Friday spikes.
[06:44] Avery: Dedicated is reserved with options for burst capacity. Pricing will be a combination of reserved monthly plus usage for burst and storage/transfer. We'll send a detailed sheet.
[06:53] Omar: Can we do a short pilot on Dedicated to validate latency and cost?
[06:56] Samir: Yes, pilot flow common: 4–6 week pilot with reduced reserved commitment, run benchmarks with your sample dataset, adjust batching/quantization profiles.
[07:05] Tom: Security review — we will need SOC2 report, penetration test summary, network diagrams, and encryption-at-rest details.
[07:12] Avery: We'll attach our SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and KMS integration docs. For Private we'll include deployment playbook.
[07:20] Priya: About latency targets again — 60–120ms for rerank is tight if cross-encoder runs per-request. We want recommended hardware shapes.
[07:28] Samir: For that SLO at 80 QPS, you'll likely need multiple GPU nodes with batching windows tuned to low latency. We'll model it: assumption examples to share — CPU vs GPU split, batch sizes N, quantized model perf.
[07:40] Maya: We can run a cost-per-query model that includes ANN cost, rerank cost, and network. Often the cheapest for tail-latency-sensitive rerank is Dedicated with local DB.
[07:51] Lena: Any gotchas with Milvus? We saw consistency issues.
[07:55] Samir: Milvus is fine at scale but needs sharding and tuning; for mission critical low tail latency, teams sometimes switch to a managed vector DB that offers SLA or push more of the hot set into Redwood cache.
[08:07] Omar: We have multi-cloud concerns — how are multi-region replicas handled?
[08:11] Maya: You can deploy Dedicated pools in multiple regions and route traffic by policy; Private you manage replication.
[08:18] Priya: For the benchmark we want: 512-dim embeddings, topK 100 recall, top50 rerank, 80 sustained QPS, spikes to 150, and include cold/warm cache scenarios.
[08:30] Samir: Noted. We'll produce a benchmark runbook. We'll need a 10k sample and representative queries.
[08:36] Lena: We'll share that by Thursday.
[08:40] Tom: On compliance, one question — can you redact query text from logs but keep metadata for audit?
[08:46] Samir: Yes, we can mask or hash query text and still emit metadata. For Private, logs remain inside your environment so you control retention.
[08:55] Maya: One more detail: model quantization can reduce memory by 2–4x with small quality drop; we recommend running a quality eval on your heldout set before shipping quantized models in production.
[09:06] Priya: We'll want to try int8 quant on the cross-encoder and maybe 8-bit for embeddings.
[09:10] Samir: We'll include quantization guidance and tooling in the follow-up.
[09:15] Avery: Quick recap and next steps?
[09:18] Maya: Recap — Marigold wants to validate Dedicated for predictable latency and to avoid cross-cloud egress; pilot benchmark for 512-dim embeddings at 80–150 QPS; share pricing, SOC2 and security docs; schedule infra deep dive.
[09:30] Lena: Sounds right. We prefer Dedicated for initial pilot and will evaluate Private for EU data residency later.
[09:36] Priya: Agree. We'll send sample dataset and query mixes.
[09:40] Tom: I'll review the security pack once you send it.
[09:44] Avery: Great. We'll follow up with the pricing sheet and benchmark plan. Thanks everyone.
[09:48] Meeting ended.

Notes about transcription: a few terms might be garbled (Redwood Optimize sometimes transcribed as Red Wood Optimize, KV cache as K-V cash), proper nouns occasionally wrong.
